---
name: failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence
description: A failing infer_instance probe says nothing about whether the fact is proved — the declaration may be a theorem, not an instance
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A failing `infer_instance` is evidence about the **instance graph**, not about
whether the mathematics is available. The declaration may exist, be proved, and
be named — just not tagged `instance`.

Case (AJCR, 2026-07-29, review-ajcr run 0082 s0006, caught before filing). Auditing
ajcr-p4's claim that `hD : LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom` is "a standard finite-type
statement carrying no Picard content", I probed
`LocallyOfFiniteType (grStructMap k d r)` by `infer_instance`. It FAILED, for both
the Grassmannian and the Grassmannian pair. I was one step from filing "p4 prices
hD as cheap and it is not available even for the ambient scheme" — a confident
refutation of a correct claim.

The facts were there all along as **theorems**: `locallyOfFiniteType_grStructMap`
(`GrassmannianScheme.lean:165`), `locallyOfFiniteType_grPairStructMap`
(`DivSchemeQProj.lean:93`), and at the carrier that actually matters a genuine
global instance `locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom` (`DivSchemeQProj.lean:199`).
`inferInstance` at `divSchemeOver` closes outright, EXIT=0. p4's pricing was right.

**Why:** the workspace's whole failure mode is confident claims about what a tree
does not contain ([[absence-claims-need-the-whole-project]],
[[private-hides-a-declaration-from-search]]). `infer_instance` adds a *new* way to
manufacture a false absence, and it is more seductive than grep because it looks
like a measurement — a probe, an EXIT code, a real elaboration. It is a real
measurement of the wrong proposition.

**How to apply:** when a probe fails, before concluding anything is missing, grep
the name and check the keyword. `theorem foo : P f` and `instance foo : P f` are
the same mathematics and different probe results. Prefer `horizon search` /
`lean_local_search` for existence, and reserve `infer_instance` for the narrow
question "is this reachable by synthesis *here*" — which is a real question
(p4's own file notes `DivRepGlobalClassify.lean` cannot see the instance because
it does not import `DivSchemeQProj`), just not the question "does this hold".

Related: [[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]] — I was auditing someone
else's price and nearly got it wrong in the *opposite* direction from usual, by
over-charging a correctly-cheap item.
